title: Generation of FLIP and FLIP-FlpE targeting vectors for conditional and reversible gene knockouts
protocol: Ensure gene inactivation after Cre recombination by inserting the cassette within the first 50% of the coding region.
Verify that both parts of the split exon remain longer than 60 bp after insertion.
Identify an overlapping or nearby CRISPR/Cas9 target sequence for the intron insertion site.
Exclude PAM sequences \(NGG) in the intron insertion site unless silent mutations are generated to prevent Cas9 binding.
Introduce several silent mutations that prevent Cas9 binding if the intron insertion site does not overlap with a CRISPR/Cas9 target sequence.
Obtain genomic sequences upstream and downstream of the intron insertion site using the UCSC genome browser.
Choose a region devoid of SapI restriction enzyme sites for both left homologous arm (LHA) and right homologous arm (RHA).
Insert the FLIP/FLIP-FlpE intronic cassette precisely between the third and last sequence of the intron insertion site.
Design forward primer (LHA-L) for LHA starting 300 – 1,000 bp upstream of the intron insertion site.
Ensure the first 3bp of the intron insertion site are the last 3bp in reverse primer (LHA-R) design for LHA.
Start forward primer (RHA-L) for RHA from the last sequence of the intron insertion site.
Design reverse primer (RHA-R) for RHA starting anywhere from 300 – 1,000 bp downstream of the intron insertion site.
Use high-fidelity polymerase for PCR amplification of homologous arms using genomic DNA from mESCs as template.
Run thermal cycler program for LHA and RHA PCR reactions.
Add DNA loading buffer to 10 μl of the PCR product.
Visualize on a 1% agarose gel at 100 V for 20 min.
Check expected band size on agarose gel.
Purify PCR products with a PCR purification kit.
Elute purified DNA in 15 μl ddH2O.
Set up the Golden Gate assembly using purified homologous arms and plasmid backbone containing either FLIP or FLIP-FlpE.
Run the specified program in a thermal cycler.
Transform 1.5 μl of reaction product into Stellar competent bacteria.
Plate the entire transformation mixture on an AMP+ (100 μg/ml) plate and incubate overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate 5 - 10 colonies from the bacterial plate and culture overnight in 2 ml of LB media supplemented with ampicillin (100 μg/ml).
Purify plasmid DNA using the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit the following day.
Perform a single EcoRI digest for left homologous arm integration.
Incubate EcoRI digest reaction for 2 hrs at 37°C.
Perform a double NotI and PstI digest for right homologous arm integration.
Incubate NotI and PstI digest reactions for 2 hrs at 37°C.
Add DNA loading dye to the digested samples.
Visualize on a 1% agarose gel at 100 V for approximately 20 minutes.
Sequence clones showing the expected pattern after digestion using specified primers.
Amplify the confirmed targeting vector by inoculating a large-scale bacterial culture.
Purify the DNA from the amplified plasmid using a Qiagen Plasmid Midi kit.
Design and order gene-specific reverse primer by concatenating the gRNA sequence in reverse complement to the binding sequence of the template vector.
Order the gene-specific reverse primer along with the common phosphorylated forward primer.
Set up the inverse PCR reaction as specified in Table 7.
Run the program detailed in Table 8 on a thermal cycler.
Add 1 μl of DpnI enzyme to the PCR product and incubate at 37°C for 2 hours.
Use 2 μl of the PCR plus DpnI mixture to initiate a ligation reaction using T4 DNA ligase as per Table 9 instructions.
Incubate the ligation mixture for 1-2 hours at room temperature.
Transform 2 μl of the ligation product into 10G competent bacteria and plate on KAN+ plates (50 μg/ml).
Incubate the plated bacteria overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate approximately 3 colonies from the bacterial plate into LB+KAN medium for overnight culture.
Isolate plasmid DNA from cultured bacteria and sequence gRNA using primers listed in Table 10.
Amplify a correct gRNA clone to be used for electroporation of mESCs with the targeting vector and Cas9 vector.
To 500 ml GMEM, add 50 ml FBS, 5 ml sodium pyruvate (1 mM), 5 ml L-Glutamine (2 mM), 5 ml MEM NEAA (1x), and 0.5 ml 2-mercaptoethanol (0.1 mM).
Store the basal medium at 4°C for up to 1 month.
To 50 ml of basal medium, add 100 μl of MLiF (20 ng/ml), 15 μl of CHIR (3 μM), and 15 μl of PD03 (1 μM).
Store the SL2i medium at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Add puromycin to a final concentration of 1 μg/ml in SL2i medium.
Prepare a 50 μg plasmid mix containing targeting vector, gRNA and Cas9 plasmids in a 1:1:1 ratio in a total volume of 80 μl in DPBS.
Coat six 10 cm dishes with 0.1% gelatin solution.
Incubate the coated plates at 37°C for >15 min.
Remove the gelatin solution and add 9 ml SL2i medium to each plate.
Keep the plates in the incubator until seeding electroporated cells.
Detach mESCs with 2 ml of Trypsin-EDTA, wash the dish with 8 ml basal medium, and collect the cells in a 50 ml tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 g for 3 min.
Resuspend cell pellet in 20 ml basal medium and count the number of cells.
Transfer 1x10^7 cells into a 15 ml tube and centrifuge at 300 g for 3 min.
Resuspend cell pellet in 800 μl DPBS.
Take 80 μl of cell suspension and plate onto one 10 cm control dish.
Add 80 μl plasmid mix to the remaining cell suspension.
Transfer the cell suspension with plasmid mix to an electroporation cuvette.
Electroporate cells using Bio-Rad Gene Pulser Xcell at 240 V voltage, 500 μF capacity, and unlimited resistance with a 4 mm cuvette.
Leave the cells at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Mix electroporated cells with 4.5 ml of SL2i medium.
Distribute 1 ml of the cell-medium mixture to each of the remaining 5 dishes.
Avoid slimy residue formed after electroporation during transfer.
Transfer dishes to a tissue culture incubator.
Start selection 48 hours post-electroporation by changing the medium to puromycin-supplemented medium.
Change the medium every second day for about 7-10 days.
Gelatinize one 96-well plate by adding 0.1% gelatin solution and incubating it in a tissue culture incubator for at least 15 minutes.
Remove the gelatin solution from the plate.
Add 100 μl selection medium per well to the gelatinized plate.
Keep the plate in an incubator until use.
Remove medium from one of the 10 cm dishes containing targeted mESC colonies.
Wash once with DPBS in the dish.
Pick mESC colonies under a light microscope using a P20 pipette set to 10 μl by scraping off the colonies while aspirating.
Transfer each picked colony to one well of a 96-well round bottom plate.
Repeat steps for the remaining dishes containing targeted mESC colonies.
Add 10 μl Trypsin-EDTA to each well and incubate at 37°C for 10 min.
Add 80 μl selection medium per well, pipette up and down 5 times to dissociate the colonies.
Transfer the cell suspension to a prepared 96-well plate containing selection medium and incubate in a tissue culture CO2 incubator.
Change the medium after 24 hours.
Gelatinize one 96-well plate.
Remove gelatin solution from the plate and add 180 μl selection medium per well, keeping the plate in an incubator until use.
Remove medium from the 96-well plate containing cells.
Wash once with DPBS and add 30 μl Trypsin-EDTA per well to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for 5-10 min.
Add 80 μl selection medium per well and mix.
Transfer 20 μl of the cell suspension to a prepared 96-well plate containing selection medium.
Place the transferred plate in an incubator.
Change the medium on the next day.
Culture the cells for 1-3 days and passage them if needed, or alternatively cryopreserve the whole plate.
Transfer the remaining 80 μl of cell suspension to a 96-well V-bottom plate.
Centrifuge the plate for 5 min at 300 g.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Add 20 μl cell lysis buffer per well.
Incubate for 2 hrs at 55°C.
Remove the plate and proceed with genotyping of the targeted mESC clones.
Dilute the DNA by 1:100 to 1:400 for preparing the PCR reaction.
Set up the PCR reaction on ice to check integration of both LHA and RHA.
Run the PCR program in a thermal cycler as specified.
Add DNA loading dye to the PCR products.
Visualize the PCR products on a 1% agarose gel.
Check for expected band size and select mESC clones positive for both arms.
Design primers that amplify approximately 500 bp of DNA around the gRNA binding sequence.
Set up the PCR reaction for mESC clones positive for LHA and RHA.
Run the PCR program in a thermal cycler as specified.
Visualize 5 μl of the PCR mix on a 1% agarose gel at 100 V, 15 min.
Confirm presence of one single band indicating successful genotyping.
Purify the PCR product using the MinElute PCR Purification Kit.
Perform Sanger sequencing analysis with the same primer used in PCR.
Culture selected mESC clones to 50-80% confluency.
Mix 3 μl Lipofectamine 2000 with 250 μl Opti-MEM and incubate for 5-10 min under the hood.
Mix 1 μg of plasmid with 250 μl Opti-MEM.
Pool the mixes from step 5.1.2 and step 5.1.3 and incubate for 20-35 min at room temperature.
Plate 2 x 10^5 cells per well in 2.5 ml SL2i medium.
Add 500 μl transfection mix per well and transfer the plates to a tissue culture incubator.
Refresh the medium the next morning.
Culture transfected cells for 2-7 days and change medium every two days.
Collect and analyze the transfected mESC clones.
